reasons: Classification is correct: affiliates are already covered without a notice condition and the licence is not revocable at will (so above walk-away), but the grant is expressly 'non-transferable' and Sections 3(c)/20(d) bar assignment with no M&A successor carve-out — that is a material failure of the stated fallback ('transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction'), so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted rather than over-flagging.

Redline is directionally correct and tracks the rule's redline guidance: it inserts contractors acting on our behalf and adds a consent-free successor-transfer right expressly overriding Sections 3(c) and 20(d), with a reasonable assumption-of-obligations proviso. Leaving the word 'non-transferable' in place is acceptable because the 'Notwithstanding' sentence controls.

The failed changed-character ratio on the second operation reflects the insertion of a new successor-transfer sentence, which is unavoidable given the fallback requirement; the edit otherwise preserves the original wording (AS400/Authorized Locations limits, additional-fee sentence) and is not an unnecessary rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, on-tone, correctly cites the playbook position and offers the M&A-limited fallback; it does not misstate the original clause.

Minor nit worth tightening (not disqualifying): the added 'in each case operating at Authorized Locations' now grammatically sweeps in Sparkling itself, whereas the original modifier attached to affiliated companies; consider 'and, in the case of such affiliated companies and contractors, operating at Authorized Locations' to avoid inadvertently narrowing our own use rights.
